newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus MPs put defence hike debate on hold.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus MPs put defence hike debate on hold.

text.p: Cypriot legislators have postponed discussions to whether to increase a defence tax on income until they are briefed by the government on a five-year military development plan, they said on Wednesday.

Members of the House of Representatives Finance and Defence Committees, who will have the final say in whether a one percentage point increase is approved or not, told journalists they wanted a briefing from the government on its military spending plans first.

"We will follow this established procedure before studying the proposed increase," Finance Committe chairman Alexis Galanos said after meeting Defence Minister Costas Eliades and Finance Minister Christodoulos Christodoulou.
Galanos said both sides agreed with the procedure.

Late last month the government submitted legislation seeking an increase in defence taxation on gross income to three from two percent. It also sought a rise in tax to four from three percent on corporate, dividend and interest earnings.
The rise aims at covering projected losses to the island's defence fund after the government agreed to suspend payments made to it by petroleum importers last July.

Importers complained they were losing money from locally controlled retail prices and soaring oil prices. The government opted for a suspension of the payment rather than approve a retail price increase, reviewed twice a year.
The move cost the fund 17 million pounds ($38.8 million).
The new five-year defence plan is due to start in 1997. The government has given no details of its cost, although media reports have estimated it at 1.2 billion Cyprus pounds.

Cyprus has engaged in a comprehensive programme to upgrade its defence capabilities for the past decade to counter the perceived threat by some 30,000 Turkish troops occupying a third of the eastern Mediterranean island.
